title: Linux on Raspberry Pi
subtitle: systemd services, cron, and running code at boot

content.text: Use systemd to run your Python script as a service, with automatic restart on failure.

content.code:
[Unit]
Description=Sensor Data Logger
After=network.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /home/pi/sensor_logger.py
WorkingDirectory=/home/pi
User=pi
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# Install and enable the service
sudo cp sensor.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable sensor.service
sudo systemctl start sensor.service

# Check status
sudo systemctl status sensor.service
journalctl -u sensor.service -f   # live logs

content.text: Use journalctl -u yourservice to view logs. This is essential for debugging headless Pi applications.

questions.question: What systemd command enables a service to start at boot?
questions.explanation: systemctl enable creates the symlink that causes the service to start automatically at boot.
